record.headline: fal doubled the price of its Flux 3 Image edit endpoint from $0.024 to $0.048 per megapixel, days after listing it.
record.who: Developers calling the Flux 3 Image edit endpoint on fal’s Model API.
record.read: A rate that doubles within days of being listed looks more like the end of an introductory price than a cost-driven hike. Newly added endpoints are the least settled lines on fal’s rate card, so teams should budget at the higher rate.
record.caveat: Social posts quoted with the PricingSaaS report describe the earlier rate as a launch promo; the report does not show fal’s page labelling it as one.

record.headline: Atlassian raised Jira Cloud Standard and Premium by about 7% per user a month at the pricing page’s default 300-user team size.
rows: Jira Standard, per user per month (300 users, monthly)
Jira Premium, per user per month (300 users, monthly)
record.who: Jira Cloud Standard and Premium customers on monthly billing at larger team sizes; the rate for small teams was not reported.
record.read: A quiet list-price rise with no notice on the page, landing on larger teams where per-seat rates are already volume-discounted. At 300 seats it adds a few hundred dollars a month, small enough to slip through at renewal.
record.caveat: Prices are for the page’s default 300-user team on monthly billing, not the small-team list rate; a later PricingSaaS capture lists Standard at $7.92 and Premium at $16.25, so the calculator output may vary.

record.headline: Atlassian raised Bitbucket Premium from $7.25 to $8 per user a month, while Standard stays at $3.65.

record.read: Arriving in the same week as the Jira increase, this looks like a coordinated autumn price move across Atlassian’s cloud products rather than a one-off. The top tier takes the rise while the entry paid tier holds.

record.short: Microsoft 365 Family and Premium storage cut from up to 6 TB (1 TB per person) to 2 TB shared; prices unchanged.
record.headline: Microsoft cut cloud storage on Microsoft 365 Family and Premium from up to 6 TB to 2 TB shared across up to 6 people, keeping prices at $129.99 and $199.99 a year.
record.who: Households on Microsoft 365 Family or Premium that share the plan with several people.
record.read: A downgrade without a price change: a full six-person household loses up to two-thirds of its storage. Heavy OneDrive users may be pushed toward extra storage purchases or separate plans.
record.caveat: PricingSaaS’s before/after table is garbled (‘up’ → ‘6 TB’); the figures come from its written summary. We capture only Microsoft’s business plans page, so this consumer change was not seen by our own pipeline.
